description: Synthetic, committed, and network-free. One corpus asked the same questions through the built-in lexical adapter and through the qmd adapter with one retrieval layer added at a time (bm25, vector, hybrid, full), so a metric that moves can be attributed to the layer that moved it rather than to one opaque pipeline. qmd's output is replayed from recordings of the real CLI: its query expansion is a language model, and its models are about 2GB that a CI machine has no business downloading. The prose and queries are inventions.

baseline.note: Layer attribution, not a regression guard for ranking constants. Measured on 2026-07-29, qmd 2.5.3: the lexical adapter and qmd's bm25 mode both ABSTAIN on the paraphrase question, whose words appear nowhere in the document that answers it — that is the gap the plan called unmeasurable, and it is now measured. vector answers it at nDCG@10 1.0000 and MRR@10 1.0000, and so, since the zero-score tie-break landed, do hybrid and full. Those two were at nDCG@10 0.3869 and MRR@10 0.2000 with the right document ranked LAST of five, and that was never a defect in the qmd adapter: relevance is a multiplicative factor in fusion, a pure paraphrase measures 0 under Recall's shared lexical definition, so every candidate in those modes scored 0, the source's own ordering was discarded, and a locator string decided the order. The tie-break fixed the ordering; it did not make the numbers mean anything. In hybrid and full every candidate here still measures relevance 0 — the four unrelated documents AND the one that answers the query — so this pack grades their rank and nothing about their scores. Two things the pack deliberately does NOT assert. It does not assert the reranked modes' off-corpus behaviour — they return unrelated documents at scores a caller cannot tell apart from a real hit, which is recorded in the adapter's search-ranked conformance transcript; asserting today's false positive as expected would make an improvement read as a regression. And it judges rank rather than relevance numbers, because a paraphrase hit's relevance is 0 by that definition and rank is what can honestly be graded. AMENDED 2026-07-29, same day, after the live rollout: vector mode now measures relevance on qmd's cosine similarity (quantized to four fixed decimals) instead of recomputing it lexically, because the lexical measure is 0 on every true paraphrase by construction and the core's relevance floor was withholding exactly the results this comparison exists to surface. The retrieval metrics above did not move: mode-vector already scored nDCG@10 1.0000 because a floor may withhold but may not abstain, so the candidate was shown either way. What moved is that it now clears the floor on its own rather than surviving a fallback, and a ninth case was added — off-corpus-vector-009 — because that mode's admission floor is qmd's own cosine threshold: a noise query returns an empty list and Recall abstains, which is the statement hybrid and full cannot make. mode-hybrid and mode-full are unchanged and still keep the lexical recompute; their scores are rank-normalized, so rank 1 is 1.0 whatever matched. RE-RECORDED 2026-07-29 for two core ranking changes and one new case, both from the epic's independent review. (1) The zero-relevance tie-break: at a fused score of zero the source's own ordering now decides instead of a locator string, which moved overall nDCG@10 0.6656 -> 0.9108 and MRR@10 0.5467 -> 0.8667, entirely from mode-hybrid and mode-full going 0.3869 -> 1.0000. mode-bm25, mode-vector, the lexical baseline tag and abstention_accuracy are unchanged, and smoke and shapes moved 0.0000 on every metric. (2) The location-scoped corroboration rule: two sources whose resolved location and record id agree are two views of one record and no longer corroborate each other. No existing case paired two sources over one location, so it moved nothing here; shared-document-views-010 is the case that exercises it, pairing the lexical adapter with the qmd vector source over the replay directory's corpus and asserting max_corroborated_units 1. That case was verified to FAIL with the rule removed (it reports 2), which is the only way to know a regression case for a scoring defect works. The document it asks about is chosen so both adapters report the same title: the name relation is the only thing that puts two sources' groups in one cluster, and a case without that agreement passes while the defect stands.
